messages.subject: Reshape data frame for choropleths plotting
parts:
Dear All,

I have a dataframe as below:

name surname    year      sex    city1      city2     city3 

AA        AAA       2011    male     10        20         30

BB        BBB       2011    female   25        15         25

CC       CCC        2012    male      16      54          32

DD       DDD        2012    female    65      41          35



I have in my ui. R two selectInput controls:

  sidebarPanel(
    
    selectInput('year', 'Year, choices= data$year),
    selectInput('gender', 'Gender', choices= data$sex)
  )


where I want to put my selected values



In my server. R I have a reactive function :



  data <- reactive({
    a <- subset(data, data$year %in% input$year)
    a <- subset(data, data$gender %in% input$gender)
    return(a)
  })


and what I want is dataframe a to be of form :


name   city       freq
 
AA       city1       10

AA      city2         20

AA      city3          30


and this data to connect with  existing .shp file with three columns:

city    long     lat

city1   ....       ....

city2   ...          ...

city3  ....     ......


in order to plot map with frequencies

Can you please help

messages.subject: Re: Reshape data frame for choropleths plotting
parts:
As Joe mentions, the question is more appropriate for a different mailing list or venue... It is not related to shiny but is concerned with how data is manipulated. Reproducible examples of your datasets would've helped along the way.

To get it going, you can try using the reshape2 or tidyr package to reshape the dataframe.

library(reshape2) # gather function from tidyr
newdata=melt(olddata,id.vars=c("name", "surname", " year", "sex")

Then rename the appropriate column to "city"

Let's assume your lat,long,city dataframe is cityloc,

newdata$lat=cityloc$lat[ match(newdata$city,cityloc$city)]# bring latitude and longitude information to main data frame
newdata$long=cityloc$long[ match(newdata$city,cityloc$city)]
 
Then use this newdata in your shiny app and subset it based on your inputs.

-Vivek
